sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:1
items.html: The expansion of the light of Ein Sof in a coupling of striking to make vessels: This is what is called the expansion of the light of Ein Sof in a coupling of striking to make vessels, for the light of Ein Sof is the secret of the light of Hochma, since only in it does the secret of striking apply, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:2
items.html: The Ruach and the Neshama are called light: This refers to the discernment of Ruach and Neshama of direct light themselves, before the ascent of the screen and its refinement from phase four to their own phases, for then there is nothing of the discernment of a vessel in them at all, since there is no vessel except from phase four; but the first three phases of direct light are considered only as causing the revelation of the vessel, namely phase four, as written (Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 15, Sub Header, "And so that") — see there. And this is what the Rav writes, "that the Ruach and the Neshama," namely phase two and phase three, "are called light," because they are not considered vessels, as clarified there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:3
items.html: Et: This alludes to the generality of the twenty-two letters from Alef to Tav, and since Malchut alone raises reflected light, and all the changes and letters and combinations of letters in the worlds come about only by cause of the reflected light, as above, it is therefore called "Et," to indicate that from it come all the distinctions, measures and boundaries.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:4
items.html: Direct light and reflected light: The meaning is, that portion of light received in the Partzuf, namely up to the Malchut, is called direct light, from above downward. And that portion of light not received in the Partzuf, namely that whole measure of upper light belonging to Malchut, which the screen within it repels and returns to its place — this portion is called reflected light, going from below upward, in such a way that direct light and reflected light are both, in fact, equally a discernment of upper light; except that the whole distinction is that this direct light is what is received in the Partzuf, while this reflected light is only the discernment of the light of departure from the vessel of Malchut — understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:5
items.html: Those Sefirot are not discernible in the Partzuf: As written above, that there is no grasp of direct light without its clothing in reflected light, and therefore those Sefirot of direct light that are above the reflected light are not discernible in the Partzuf, even though they are present there. For example, in reflected light reaching the stature of Bina, Keter and Hochma are not discernible in that Partzuf, even though they clothe within the interiority of Bina — understand this. (See Ohr Pnimi above, Chapter 3, Item 6.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:6
items.html: They suffice only for the vessels of the head: That is, by the clothing of the ten Sefirot of direct light in the reflected light ascending from the screen from below upward, they suffice only for the discernment of the vessels of the head, meaning only roots for vessels, and not complete vessels. (As above, Ohr Pnimi, Chapter 5, Item 20.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:7
items.html: The complete vessels, called Guf: That is, after the reflected light overturns and descends from the screen downward, when the Malchut, which is "the mouth," widens and expands into ten Sefirot from itself and within itself (as above, Ohr Pnimi, Chapter 2, Item 3), down to the Malchut within it, called "the Nefesh of the mouth" — then complete vessels are made, called "Guf," or the ten Sefirot of the Guf.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:8
items.html:
By the light of gazing and Malchut, which strikes and returns the light: The meaning is, by the light of gazing, which is the secret of the expansion of the light of Ein Sof, and by Malchut, which is the secret of the screen that strikes and returns the light backward, these two participate together in the making of the vessels, as clarified.
And one must know the secret of the second gazing mentioned here, which is the secret of the ascent of the lights to the Emanator (mentioned in Etz Chaim, Gate of Akudim, Chapter 3, and below, Part 4, Chapter 4), the meaning of which is the refinement of the screen from phase four to phase three, and so on, until its refinement to the phase of root, called the Emanator, so that in the course of its departure it makes all five stature-levels, called the five vessels: KHB, ZA, and Malchut, of the Guf.
For the first expansion, up to the Nefesh of the mouth, makes the vessel of Keter of the Guf. And when Malchut ascends to ZA, that is, when phase four is refined to phase three, a second coupling of striking is made, and it brings forth the stature of Hochma, and thereby the vessel of Hochma of the Guf is made. And when Malchut ascends to phase two, in the same manner as above, the vessel of Bina of the Guf is made. And when Malchut ascends to phase one, in the same manner as above, the vessel of ZA of the Guf is made. And when Malchut ascends to its own root phase, that is, when it is refined of all the coarseness that was in it, the vessel of Malchut of the Guf is made.
And this is what the Rav writes, that by the second gazing of the coupling of striking, in the screen that is in the Malchut of the expansion of the mouth, the reflected light again ascends from below upward, until it departs entirely, whereby the ten Sefirot KHB, ZA and Malchut of the Guf are made.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:9
items.html: The discernment of Malchut went out first: That is, in the discernment of the ten Sefirot of reflected light we find that Malchut went out first, for it is the source and root of the whole of the ten Sefirot of reflected light, since all this reflected light is, itself, the very portion that it should have received, were it not for the screen that restrains it. And therefore Malchut is regarded as the discernment of root and Keter for the whole of the ten Sefirot of reflected light, which it includes, all of them. And this is what is written, "the discernment of Malchut went out first," that is, in the discernment of reflected light, as clarified.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:10
items.html: The stature of all the Sefirot is equal: For direct light is ordered from above downward, meaning from the pure to the coarse, so that the purer something is, the more important it is. And the opposite is true of reflected light, which is ordered from below upward, meaning from the coarse to the pure, so that the coarser something is, the more important it is. Therefore, when they clothe one another, all are found equal: for whatever is lowest in direct light — Malchut, for example — is found highest in reflected light, since Malchut is the Keter of reflected light, and so too the reverse; and it therefore follows that Keter and Malchut are equal in stature, and so with the rest of the Sefirot, since a deficiency in direct light is always an advantage and superiority in reflected light, and so the reverse, and therefore all the ten Sefirot are equal in stature. (See in the Inner Observation here, Chapter 3, where this is clarified at length.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:11
items.html: Yesod has something of the direct light above it: That is, although Yesod has something of the direct light above it, called "before it," whereas Malchut receives nothing at all of the upper light before it, since the screen restrains it and returns it entirely upward, nevertheless the two are equal, as is explained further.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:12
items.html: By the great abundance of the reflected light of Malchut, Yesod received power: That is, by the great abundance of the reflected light of Malchut, Yesod received power to expand beyond its measure, since by the power of this reflected light it reached the stature of Keter, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:13
items.html:
Yet with respect to the vessels themselves, they are equal: That is, its whole superiority over Malchut is because Malchut is reflected light without direct light, meaning light of departure from Malchut, which returns and draws near to its root; whereas Yesod receives its portion of direct light, which is certainly a great superiority. Nevertheless, on the side of the vessels themselves, namely the reflected light, they are equal, meaning that after this departing reflected light ascended and clothed all the Sefirot and became a vessel for them, as above, from this side they are both equal, since all the direct light that is grasped in the Partzuf is only by cause of this reflected light, and no Sefira of direct light can illuminate the Partzuf without it; thus direct light and reflected light both join equally in the illumination of the Partzuf.
And you must remember here what the Rav wrote earlier (this chapter, Item 3), that direct light and reflected light are both, in fact, one and the same light, namely the light of gazing, except that all the inferiority of reflected light is that it is light of departure from Malchut; whereas now, on the contrary, the whole expansion of the light in general depends on and is bound up with reflected light, and it is therefore now, for this reason, entirely equal to direct light, since it has now become, again, a discernment of the light of expansion, in that it has become vessels — understand this well. And this is what the Rav writes: "but with respect to the vessels themselves, they are equal."

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:14
items.html: A copyist's error: There is a copyist's error here, and it should read, "and when the breath returns and clothes the light," for the breath, which is the secret of reflected light, clothes the direct light, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:15
items.html: The mouth is the root of reflected light: For the mouth is the root of reflected light, and is therefore the head, that is, the Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:12:16
items.html: The reflected light reaching the ear, which is Bina: For the reflected light reaching the ear, which is Bina, is the Sefira of Hod of reflected light, which is a discernment of the Guf. (See here in the Inner Observation, Chapter 3, where this is clarified at length.)
